_readme: The editorial half of this repository's self-description: what cannot be derived from the code. Structure and import boundaries are NOT here -- they are enforced by tests/test_boundaries.py against the real import graph. An earlier version also described directories, invariants and generated-file provenance; all of it duplicated something computed elsewhere, and four of those copies had already gone stale. If a fact can be checked by a test, it belongs in the test, not here.

repo.name: ha-godox-mesh
repo.what: A Home Assistant (HACS) custom integration for Godox Bluetooth-mesh lights, the Python library it wraps, and the reverse-engineering research both were derived from -- in one repository.
repo.upstream: mattharrison/godox-ul60bi-bt (the library and CLI; this fork adds the integration)

renamed_from.note: Rename is uncommitted in the working tree at time of audit; `git status` shows the moves as staged renames. Residual old-name strings are listed in the audit.

repo.distribution: Installed through HACS, never from PyPI. The library is vendored into the integration rather than declared as a requirement -- manifest.json `requirements` is deliberately empty.

derivations.guard: tests_ha/test_capabilities_generated.py -- regenerates from the committed artifacts and asserts the result matches. Needs no vendor material, so it runs in CI.
tests_ha/test_vendored_lib.py -- runs in CI (.github/workflows/hacs.yml) and fails on drift in either direction

known_gaps: firmware-measurements.json cannot be regenerated in CI -- it is measured from Godox firmware images, which are not redistributable. It is not underivable, though: reverse-artifacts/fetch_firmware.py downloads the corpus from Godox's own endpoint using the URLs and sizes in the committed firmware-coverage.json, so the chain is reproducible by anyone with a network connection. What CI checks instead is the half that is joined from committed artifacts (versions, product names), via tests/test_firmware_measurements.py.
custom_components/, tests_ha/ and tools/ are not type checked anywhere
tools/ is not mentioned in the top-level README

Colour (HSI/RGBW), gels, tint and the newer 0xF7 effect frame have never run against hardware -- both available lights are bi-colour, effectVersion 0, no tint, no gels. The frames themselves are read byte-for-byte out of the vendor app and asserted as such, so the risk is not in the framing. It is in three inferences: the 0-255 -> 0-1000 channel rescale (this repository's choice, not Godox's), the gel number being the catalogue's sortNum (inferred from the app's lookup, not read from an assignment), and each model being classified into the right frame format from catalogue fields that the protocol cannot confirm. See docs/model-support.md.
CIE xy (0xFA) is implemented in the library but not advertised as a Home Assistant colour mode: all 40 models that accept it also accept HSI, and Home Assistant derives xy_color from any colour mode.
The V3 effects take per-effect parameters beyond speed (trigger, mode, colour-block lists). They are sent at the vendor app's own defaults (FX_V3_DEFAULTS); none is exposed as an entity.

Pixel-light animations (1 model), electronic accessory control (12) and selfie colour temperature (2) are not implemented -- see docs/model-support.md for why each is out of scope rather than pending.
